behavior: Commit one immutable local purchase identity, then submit with the same supplier key outside the transaction.

input.name: productId
input.constraint: nonempty reference; existence is not checked here

input.name: unitPrice
input.constraint: 0..9999999999999999.99; rounding to two decimal places leaves the numeric value unchanged

input.name: provider
input.constraint: direct | wiremock | microcks, exact named value

sourceBinding.status: source-reconciled specification; no current runtime or compliance verdict

domainModelNotes: No Procurement domain-event object is emitted. GoodsReceived is a separate producer-owned integration contract on first receipt.
steps: Validate identity before database or supplier I/O; generate candidate Guid.NewGuid() and UTC timestamp.
CreateOrGetAsync enforces unique ClientRequestId and returns the committed aggregate; RequireIdentity rejects any changed field before supplier POST.
If the existing order is already settled, return it without another POST. Created describes local first creation only.
For PendingSubmission or SubmissionUnknown, POST original supplier identity; apply a validated known outcome under the submission committer lock.
failureSemantics: Ordinary SupplierGatewayException including timeout/unavailable/invalid response marks unsettled state SubmissionUnknown using CancellationToken.None and returns it.
supplier_identity_conflict and supplier_business_rejection propagate after the local identity commit; a newly created order can remain PendingSubmission.
Caller cancellation during submission marks unknown with CancellationToken.None and rethrows; failures before the identity commit do not imply a durable order.
Concurrent pending same-key calls can each send HTTP; upstream idempotency is required for one logical supplier order.
postconditions: Never increment stock or stage GoodsReceived merely because a supplier accepted.
Same key with changed product/provider/SKU/quantity/price/currency conflicts; immutable identity is not silently overwritten.
